Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("(μ, ξ) := (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, ξ_v) … is an admissible representation of C … (0, 0) represents ∂C = 0. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, this data, f, L := 1 … ISP of C … gives an L¹-null set N such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N"), together with step 1 (∂C = 0) and the formula of step 3, both supplied by the sibling plane_stokes (PS). Also uses the siblings plane_measure (PM) and covector_eval_le (O1).

1. (Representation of C.) Let μ := θ₀·(Hⁿ⌞V₀) (the scalar ENNReal.ofReal θ₀; θ₀ > 0), ξ_v ∈ Λ_n the evaluation at v, ξ_v(α) := α(v_0, …, v_d) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v), and ξ(x) := ξ_v for all x.
   (a) μ is finite on compact sets: by (PM)(iii) with m := n, w := v, a := 0 (where {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} = V₀), Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞, hence μ(K) = θ₀Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞.
   (b) ξ is constant, hence a.e. strongly measurable, and |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(v)| ≤ |α| for every α by (O1) (v is orthonormal).
   (c) For every test n-form ω, ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) = (ENNReal.ofReal θ₀).toReal·∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = C(ω) (integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).

2. (∂C = 0 and its representation.) For a test d-form η, ∂C(η) = C(dη) = θ₀∫_{V₀}dη(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀·0 = 0 by (PS)(a). Take μ′ := 0 and ξ′ := 0: μ′ is finite, ξ′ is constant, the bound holds trivially (μ′-a.e. statements are vacuous for μ′ = 0), and ∫ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′ = 0 = ∂C(η).

3. (The slicing function.) f(y) := ⟨y, v_0⟩ is 1-Lipschitz: |f(y) − f(y′)| = |⟨y − y′, v_0⟩| ≤ ‖y − y′‖·‖v_0‖ = ‖y − y′‖ (Cauchy–Schwarz, ‖v_0‖ = 1).

4. (Slices from (SL).) Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (open), k := d, T := C, the data (μ, ξ), (μ′, ξ′) of steps 1–2 (finiteness on compact subsets of U by step 1(a)), f of step 3 and L := 1. This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′(x) for all t and test forms; only these two formulas are used.

5. (Integer multiplicity from ISP.) The hypotheses of ISP for (μ, ξ), (μ′, ξ′), f, L = 1 are exactly steps 1–3. Hence there is an L¹-null set N such that for t ∉ N every pair (A, B) with the two integral formulas has ∂A − B integer multiplicity. For t ∉ N the pair (A_t, B_t) of step 4 qualifies, so Z := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity. (Lean: filter_upwards on the ∀ᵐ t given by ISP.)

6. (Formula for Z.) Fix t ∉ N and a test d-form φ. By the contract's subtraction of currents and ∂A(φ) = A(dφ), Z(φ) = A_t(dφ) − B_t(φ). Here B_t(φ) = ∫ … d(μ′⌞{f<t}) = 0 since μ′ = 0 (Measure.restrict_zero, integral_zero_measure). The half-space {f < t} is open, hence Borel, so μ⌞{f<t} = θ₀·Hⁿ⌞({f<t} ∩ V₀) (Measure.restrict_smul, Measure.restrict_restrict) and
   A_t(dφ) = θ₀∫_{V₀∩{⟨y,v_0⟩<t}} dφ(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(v_1, …, v_d)dH^d(y)
   by (PS)(b). Hence Z(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(Fin.tail v)dH^d(y) for every test d-form φ, for every t ∉ N, i.e. for L¹-a.e. t. ∎
